title: feat(notifications): deliver inbox notifications to devices via Expo push (C-643-2)
body:
## Tier header

- **Tier:** T4
- **Why:** this sends real lock-screen pushes to users' phones (personal data: names and appointment times) for every inbox notification that previously reached no device, and it changes what the inbox and unread badge return to installed builds. Continuation of B-FLAGS-3 for #643 (Opus C-643-2, Sol B-643-1 and B-643-2).
- **T4 trigger scan:** user-facing device delivery and lock-screen copy; token invalidation (it writes `users.expo_push_token`); a migration `20270307000000_push_outbox_quiet_hours` (new backend-only table `PushOutbox`, round 3 adds the nullable `time_zone`, `lease_token`, `handed_off_at` columns in the same unapplied migration, with forced RLS, anon/authenticated denied, service_role bypass, FK cascade from User; `Notification.inbox_hidden` + a one-time backfill of proven twins); the inbox and unread counts installed builds read. Carries #647's T4 items (its migration, `PUT /notifications/timezone`, `prisma/schema-parity-baseline.sql`). No auth, billing, env or workflow change.
- **T4 (deletion):** adds one `account-deletion.manifest.ts` entry (`PushOutbox.user_id`, erase).
- **T3 trigger scan:** two crons (`push-outbox` every minute: lease expiry + drain that leases ONE row at a time with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, every worker write fenced by `lease_token`, the lease renewed and `handed_off_at` stamped in one CAS right before the Expo call (round 3); `push-receipts` every 5 min: receipts from the outbox rows + 30-day retention), a new DI provider, and three writers (first payment, drip, purchase fan-out) that now mark their `push` twin rows.
- **Bounded T1:** none.
- **Builder-owner:** B-FLAGS-3 continuation (agent 112); round 2 by B-NOTIF-5 (agent 114); rounds 3-4 by B-NOTIF-6 (agent 115, Claude Opus 5.5 builder). Builders never audit their own change.
- **Acceptance evidence:** see below.
- **Promotion triggers:** n/a (already T4).

**#647 is merged** (main d23fa317, merged into this branch in round 4 at 22de1182), so this diff is this PR's own. Historical note: the branch carried #647 (base `main`, merged up to 0d33c4d4 in round 4; this branch merges #647's head df4eb80b). Merge #647 first; this diff then reduces to this PR's own commits. One migration (`20270307000000`, prefix to be confirmed by the operator), no new env names and no package.json change (`expo-server-sdk` 6.1.0 stays, for its types and `isExpoPushToken`).

## Verification first (main 3bd6215b, read-only)

The claim is confirmed: push-channel notifications are stored but never sent.
- `createNotification` (`notifications.service.ts:297-354`) checks preferences and a 60 s throttle, then only inserts a row. Nothing reads `channel:'push'` rows. The coach-AI `send-notification` materialiser even claims a pipeline polls them, but none exists.
- Expo is called only in `pushToCoach` (:480) and `pushToUser` (:542). These emitters wrote an `inapp` row and a `push` twin and never reached a device: booking (all 7 kinds, reminders included), message-received (coach messages), milestone-reached, weight-trend-alert, checkin-submitted, missed-checkin, build-week-day-unlocked. Coach-alert pushed through `pushToCoach`, with the alert text as the lock-screen title, and also wrote a twin.
- The welcome message is #609 and is not on main, so there is nothing to wire here. When it lands, it should call `sendPush`.
- Paths that already send (left unchanged): community, drip, purchase fan-out, package push, nudges, churn, coach brief, dunning, scout.
- Token registration works: `PATCH /users/me/push-token` (`users.controller.ts:171`), and mobile calls `getExpoPushTokenAsync`. Android has no FCM V1 key in Expo yet, so Expo answers Android sends with `InvalidCredentials`.
- The old `pollReceipts` polls immediately after the send (receipts are not ready yet). It also clears a user's token by `userId` without matching the token, and logs at error level per push. A missing FCM key would therefore cause an error storm on those paths. This PR leaves those paths as they are and builds the new sender correctly; moving them onto it is a separate small follow-up.

## Fix round 1 (agent 112)

| Finding | Change | Commit | Test (fails before: the module or method does not exist on main, or main writes 2 rows) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opus C-643-2 / Sol B-643-1: no device delivery | New `PushDeliveryService` (Expo Push API): token lookup and Expo-token validation, one send, at most once with no retry storm. The SDK's own bounded 429 retry still applies. It never throws. `NotificationsService.sendPush` is gated by `muted` and `<kind>_push`, like the row, and writes no row. | 81c52a12 | `test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts` "sends one message ...", "transport failure ..." |
| Receipts | Ticket ids queue in a bounded in-memory list (5,000). The `push-receipts` cron checks them after 2 min or more, keeps them up to 24 h, and retries a failed fetch on the next sweep. | 81c52a12 | "receipts: checked after a delay ..." |
| Token invalidation | `DeviceNotRegistered` on a ticket or receipt runs `updateMany where { id, expo_push_token: <that token> }`, so a newer registration is never wiped. | 81c52a12 | "DeviceNotRegistered on the ticket ...", receipts case |
| Android without the FCM key | `InvalidCredentials`: the token is kept and the send is dropped. One `PUSH_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED` operator alert per hour per process says how to fix it (upload the FCM V1 key with `eas credentials`). iOS is unaffected. No error storm. | 81c52a12 | "Android without the FCM key ..." |
| Per-user rate limits | 1 per user per kind per 60 s, and at most 8 per user per 10 min. In-process and bounded (pruned past 20k users). | 81c52a12 | "rate limits ..." |
| Quiet lock-screen copy | `lock-screen-copy.ts`: booking kinds keep the name and local time (from #647). Messages say "New message from X", never the text. Weight, milestone, check-in, missed check-in, coach alert, build-week, workout and meal plan get fixed quiet copy ("There is a new update on your progress. Open the app to see it."). Unknown kinds get a generic line. There are no emojis or exclamation marks. Tap data is `actionScreen` (Messages or NotificationCenter) plus the id-only deep link. | 81c52a12 | "never puts health detail ...", "booking and message copy ...", "sends quiet lock-screen copy ..." |
| Emitters wired | booking, message-received, milestone-reached, weight-trend-alert, checkin-submitted, missed-checkin (client and coach) and build-week now write one `inapp` row and call `sendPush`. Coach-alert writes one `inapp` row and calls `sendPush` instead of `pushToCoach` plus the twin. | 81c52a12 | `test/notification-emitters.spec.ts` (1 row plus 1 push each), `test/booking-emitter.spec.ts` (each reminder pushed once) |
| Sol B-643-2: one inbox item, installed builds included | `listNotifications`, its unread count and `getUnreadCount` hide `channel:'push'` rows of the 17 twin kinds (`PUSH_TWIN_KINDS`). This also hides twins already stored, and old app builds get it because only the API response changes. Push-only kinds (community, workout and meal-plan assignment, coach-AI) stay visible. | 81c52a12 | "the inbox and unread count hide stored push twins ..." |
| Sol: prove one push per eligible participant, zero when opted out | Real `BookingEmitter`, `NotificationsService` and `PushDeliveryService` with only Expo mocked. Each reminder is claimed once in `NotificationDeliveryLog` (#647), so it is pushed once. | 81c52a12 | "one push to each eligible participant ...", "zero pushes when ... opted out ..." |

## Fix round 2 (B-NOTIF-5, agent 114)

Design change: every device push is now one row in a durable `PushOutbox`. `sendPush` writes the row (in the caller's transaction when there is one) and returns; a worker leases due rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and sends them with a cancelling deadline. Nothing in a request waits on Expo.

| Finding | Change | Commit | Test (fails on 81c52a12) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opus+Sol B-648-1: the per-kind throttle dropped distinct reminders and messages; the 8 / 10 min cap dropped pushes | No in-memory throttle. A booking event has an exactly-once `dedupe_key` (kind, session, start time), so two sessions never collide and two replicas never double-send. Repeats in one conversation collapse (an unsent push takes the newest copy; a repeat within 60 s of a sent one folds into it; the inbox row is still written). The per-user cap (8 per 10 min) now DEFERS non-urgent pushes to when the window has room; booking events are exempt. Nothing is dropped by a rate limit. | de2a78fc | `test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts` "two 1 h reminders for different sessions ... both pushed", "the same reminder enqueued twice ... pushed once", "two messages in the same thread within 60 s give one push; two threads give two", "past the burst cap ... deferred ..., then sent", "urgent reminders are exempt from the burst cap" |
| Sol B-648-6: no deadline on Expo calls; the booking call and the serial sweep waited on Expo | `sendPush` only enqueues. `FetchExpoPushClient` calls the two documented Expo endpoints with a caller-owned AbortSignal (`expo-server-sdk`'s client takes none); sends abort at 10 s, receipt fetches at 15 s, and the request is really cancelled. A timed-out send is not retried (Expo may have accepted it: at most once). HTTP 429/5xx (not accepted) retries with backoff (30 s, 2 min) up to 3 attempts. A row left `sending` by a dead process is closed at lease expiry, never re-sent. | de2a78fc | "sendPush returns while the Expo send never settles; the stalled send is aborted at the deadline", "a stalled receipt fetch is aborted and releases the sweep latch", "HTTP 503 ... retried with backoff, then dropped after MAX_ATTEMPTS", "the fetch transport passes the signal and classifies HTTP errors", "a row left `sending` by a dead process is closed at lease expiry" |
| Sol B-648-7: the kind-only twin filter hid sole push rows (coach-AI) | `Notification.inbox_hidden`. Only a proven twin is hidden: the three writers that store a twin (first payment, drip, purchase fan-out) pass `push_twin: true`; the migration backfills stored twins (a `push` row within 10 s of an `inapp` row with the same user, kind, deep link and text, never a coach-AI row). The inbox and both unread counts filter `inbox_hidden = false`. | de2a78fc | "B-648-7: a proven push twin is hidden; a sole push row of a listed kind stays visible" |
| Opus C-648-4 / OR-113-5: quiet hours not enforced | 21:00-08:00 in the recipient's zone (`resolveRecipientTimeZone`, provenance from #647), one window definition (`QuietHoursPolicy`). Non-urgent pushes wait until 08:00 local. Urgent bypass: the 1 h reminder, and any booking event whose session (old or new time) starts before 08:00 local + 2 h. A deferred reminder is re-checked when sent (session still scheduled at that time, still ahead) and its lock-screen line is rendered then ("today"). No known zone: sent now, never guessed. | de2a78fc | "a message at 23:00 New York waits until 08:00 New York; Tokyo (noon) is sent now", "urgent bypass ...", "a deferred 24 h reminder is re-rendered at 08:00 ("today"), and dropped if the session was cancelled" |
| Opus C-648-5: receipts in memory | Receipts are read from the outbox rows (`ticket_id`, `sent_at`, `receipt_checked_at`) 2+ minutes after the send, so a restart loses none. Rows are deleted after 30 days. | de2a78fc | "receipts survive a restart: a new process reads them from the outbox and clears a dead token" |
| Opus C-648-2: `@Optional()` push delivery hid a DI miss | `NotificationsService.onModuleInit` throws in production when PushDeliveryService is missing (logs an error elsewhere). Thin unit tests that build the service by hand never run the hook. | de2a78fc | "C-648-2: a production boot without PushDeliveryService fails loudly" |
| Android without the FCM V1 key | `InvalidCredentials` keeps the token and records the push as `provider-not-configured`, never as sent; one `PUSH_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED` line per hour per process. iOS is unaffected. No Android delivery is claimed until the owner uploads the key. | de2a78fc | "InvalidCredentials keeps the token, never records the push as sent, and alerts once an hour" |
| Inherited Sol B-647-1 / B-647-2, Opus B-647-1, C-647-2, C-647-3 | Closed in #647 (head df4eb80b) and merged here. | ee66b618, 9f560fa8 | see #647 FIX ROUND 3 |
| #608 erasure manifest (main ec911328) | `PushOutbox.user_id` erased with the account (`del`, FK-safe: child of User, cascades). | 16294f44 | `test/account-deletion/erasure-manifest-coverage.spec.ts` (failed before with `PushOutbox.user_id` uncovered), `manifest-fk-order.spec.ts` |
| Opus C-648-3: booking pushes open the list, not the session | Backend half: push `data` now carries `sessionId` next to the deep link. The tap still targets `NotificationCenter` because the mobile allow-list has no session screen yet; a `SessionDetail` route is a mobile follow-up. | de2a78fc | n/a (data field only; the tap target change is mobile) |

Kept from round 1: lock-screen privacy (no health detail, no message text), exact-token compare-and-set clearing, preference gating (`muted`, `<kind>_push`), one inbox row per event, emitters wired.

## Fix round 3 (B-NOTIF-6, agent 115)

Findings at 16294f44: Sol RC (B-648-8, B-648-9, B-648-10, C-648-3 carried). Opus had no verdict at that head. Tests are in `test/push-delivery-send-time.spec.ts` (new) unless noted. Failing before: the tests-only commit on 16294f44 in the one-job CI lane, https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37142172833 (10 failed, 4 passed; the 4 that pass are lock-screen and urgency verification, not findings).

| Finding | Change | Commit | Test (fails on 16294f44) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sol B-648-8 (a batch outlived its lease; a second worker re-sent rows) | The worker leases ONE row at a time just before sending (`claimNext`: LIMIT 1, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, fresh `lease_token`). Every worker write is a compare-and-set on `{id, status 'sending', lease_token}`. Right before the Expo call, `handOff` renews the lease and stamps `handed_off_at` in one CAS; if it fails the row is not sent (`lease-lost`). `expireLeases`: a lapsed claim that was never handed off goes back to pending (attempt refunded, `lease-released`); a lapsed handed-off row is closed `lease-expired`, never re-sent. `finish` honours the CAS count. Receipts: CAS on `receipt_checked_at: null`, counted only when this replica wrote it. Drain bounded by `MAX_ROWS_PER_DRAIN` 500. | a41b4c47 | "Sol's probe: 15 rows, 9 s per provider reply, a second worker sweeps at 126 s; every row is sent once and recorded"; "a claim that lapses before the handoff goes back to the queue; the stalled worker does not send it, the other sends it once"; "two replicas reading the same receipts count each receipt once"; existing `push-delivery.service.spec.ts` dead-process case now sets `handed_off_at` |
| Sol B-648-9 (a push queued before "mute all" or a switch-off still went out) | New `src/notifications/push/push-preferences.ts`: `notificationPrefsPrefix` (moved from NotificationsService, which delegates) and `pushAllowedByPreferences(prefs, kind)`. `sendOne` re-reads `notificationPreferences` before the send; off → dropped `preference-off`. `sendPush` uses the same helper. | a41b4c47 | "\"mute all\" turned on while a night message waits: nothing reaches the phone at 08:00"; "the message switch turned off while a push waits suppresses it; booking pushes still go" |
| Sol B-648-10 (quiet hours decided only at enqueue) | `sendOne` re-resolves the recipient zone (`resolveRecipientTimeZone`, fallback the row's new `time_zone`) and re-applies `quietHoursFor` at send: inside the window → deferred to 08:00 local (`quiet_hours`, `quiet-deferred`) without spending an attempt. `urgent` is the caller's explicit urgency only; the burst-cap exemption is computed at send. Lock-screen times render in the current zone. An error before the handoff is a bounded `worker_retry`; after it, `transport-error` (never re-sent). | a41b4c47 | "queued at 20:59 New York, the worker reaches it at 23:00: it waits until 08:00, then is sent"; "a provider retry that lands after 21:00 waits for the morning without spending an attempt"; "the recipient moved to Los Angeles while the push waited ..."; "a booking confirmation for a session days away, queued at 20:59 and reached at 23:00, waits for the morning" |
| C-648-3 (tap did not open the session) | `pushTapData`: a booking push names the recipient's side, the same contract as backend #634 (`BOOKING_PUSH_SCREEN`) and mobile #325/#341: client `CalendarSession`, coach `CoachBookingInbox`, both with `actionParams.sessionId` (side read from the session's `coach_id`/`client_id`; unknown → notification center). Messages open `Messages`. `deepLink` and top-level `sessionId` kept for older builds; an unknown screen falls back to the notification center on device. | a41b4c47, ab607b34 (test 811777c2) | "the client's push opens CalendarSession and the coach's opens CoachBookingInbox, both with the session id" |
| Verification (lane brief: coach messages reach the lock screen) | No change needed: a coach message (the #609 welcome is one) is pushed with title "New message", body "New message from <coach>", sound default, high priority, opens Messages; at 21:30 local it waits and is sent at 08:00. | — | "a coach message (the welcome is one) is pushed to the client with quiet copy that opens Messages"; "a welcome sent at 21:30 the client's time waits and reaches the lock screen at 08:00" (pass before and after) |

Schema: `PushOutbox` gains nullable `time_zone`, `lease_token`, `handed_off_at`, added in place to `20270307000000_push_outbox_quiet_hours/migration.sql` (unapplied in every environment; the down migration still drops the table) and `prisma/schema.prisma`. Test fake `test/utils/push-outbox-fake.ts` models the one-row claim, lease token and preferences.

## Fix round 4 (B-NOTIF-6, agent 115) — head 22de1182, 11/11 required checks green

Finding at ab607b34: Sol RC 0/1/0 (B-648-10 partial, comment 5972046897). Opus had no verdict at ab607b34. Failing before: tests-only commit 12ebc6b3 (= ab607b34 + tests) in the one-job CI lane, https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37143855203 (3 failed, 15 passed).

| Finding | Change | Commit | Test (fails on ab607b34) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sol B-648-10 partial (the window was judged on the clock read when `sendOne` began; a slow read inside the lease carried a non-urgent push past 21:00) | No `now` captured at entry. The obsolete-reminder check, the quiet check and the burst window each read the clock after the awaited reads. After the handoff CAS a second fresh clock (`sendAt`) re-checks the window: inside it, the row goes back to pending for 08:00 (`quiet_hours`, attempt refunded, `handed_off_at` and lease cleared) and Expo is not called. `sendAt` renders the lock-screen copy and is recorded as `sent_at`. Urgency exceptions and 21:00-08:00 unchanged. | ba6a2c76 (tests eb55a9b3, 12ebc6b3) | "Sol's probe: the token read ends at 21:00:10, so nothing is sent; it waits for 08:00 without spending an attempt"; "the handoff write itself ends after 21:00: the row never reached Expo, so it goes back for 08:00"; "daytime control: a 70 s read at 14:00 still sends, and the row records the handoff time". Control passing before and after: "urgent control: a 1 h reminder whose reads cross 21:00 is still sent" |
| Merge-only (DIRTY against main 0d33c4d4 after #609) | Merge commit. One conflict, `NotificationsService._kindToPrefsPrefix`: kept the delegation to `push-preferences.ts` and added #609's `workout_reminder` mapping there, so the enqueue and send-time gates read `workout_reminder_*`. | ef0ad6fc | `test/engagement/workout-reminder.service.spec.ts` 32/32 locally; full suite in required checks |

Local (heavy.sh, one file each): `test/push-delivery-send-time.spec.ts` 18/18, `test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts` 22/22. eslint clean; check-r75 OK.

## Acceptance evidence (round 3)

- Local (heavy.sh, one file each): `test/push-delivery-send-time.spec.ts` 14/14; `test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts` 22/22. eslint clean on changed files. `node scripts/check-r75.js --mode=range --base=origin/main --head=HEAD`: OK.
- Required checks at the head (full suite, tsc, schema parity, live suites): see the FIX ROUND 3 comment.

## Acceptance evidence (round 2)

- `heavy.sh npx jest --runInBand --forceExit test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts`: 22/22.
- `heavy.sh npx jest --runInBand --forceExit` over push-delivery, drip-dispatcher.cron, booking-emitter, first-payment-webhook / -tx-rollback / -throttle-rollback, coach-new-purchase-prefs-routing: 7 suites, 79/79. Earlier in the round: notification-emitters, booking-reminder-local-time, notification-timezone-provenance, notification-local-time, booking-reminder.job, notification-prefs, audit-phase10, nudge-v1-prefs-and-copy, notifications-category, voice-policy-empty-notifications, coach-alerts-emitters, coach-alerts-push-delivery, notifications.controller: all pass.
- Failing before: on 81c52a12 `PushDeliveryService.enqueue`, `FetchExpoPushClient`, `quietHoursFor`, `PushOutbox` and `inbox_hidden` do not exist, and the old service dropped the second reminder and the ninth push (its own tests asserted the drop).
- `node scripts/check-r75.js --mode=range --base=origin/main --head=HEAD`: OK (`as never` net -14). eslint clean on every changed file.
- Local full tsc runs out of memory in the shared sandbox; CI build-and-test is the verifier.

## Not in this PR (for the operator)

- Migration prefix `20270307000000` was chosen as the first prefix after the annex reservation (20270301-20270306); please confirm. Round 3 edited it in place (three nullable columns); it is unapplied in every environment, so no new migration was added.
- #634 also rewrites `booking.emitter.ts`; whichever of #634/#648 merges second resolves that file. The booking tap contract is already the same in both (client `CalendarSession`, coach `CoachBookingInbox`, `actionParams.sessionId`).
- A queued message push is not re-checked against a block made after it was queued (the outbox has no sender id; `messaging.service.ts` overlaps #609). Candidate follow-up.
- Android delivery needs the FCM V1 key (owner task); no Android delivery claim is made.
- Mobile follow-up (B-NOTIF-6, one mobile PR): send the device zone with `PUT /notifications/timezone` on sign-in and foreground, a `SessionDetail` tap target for the `actionScreen`/`actionParams.sessionId` this PR now sends, and a Quiet hours screen that states the enforced 21:00-08:00 window instead of the nested `quietHours` payload the DTO strips.
- `pushToUser` / `pushToCoach` (community, drip, purchase, dunning, nudges ...) still send directly; moving them onto the outbox is a separate follow-up.
- `EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN` is not used (same as the existing senders).

No merge, workflow dispatch or production action by the builder.
